{{Short description|Operation selecting specific components or columns from a set, tuple, or relation}}
In [[set theory]], a '''projection''' is one of two closely related types of [[function (mathematics)|function]]s or operations, namely:

* A [[set theory|set-theoretic]] operation typified by the <math>j</math><sup>th</sup> projection map, written <math>\mathrm{proj}_j,</math> that takes an element <math>\vec{x} = (x_1,\ \dots,\ x_j,\ \dots,\ x_k)</math> of the [[Cartesian product]] <math>(X_1 \times \cdots \times X_j \times \cdots \times X_k)</math> to the value <math>\mathrm{proj}_j(\vec{x}) = x_j.</math><ref>{{citation|title=Naive Set Theory|series=[[Undergraduate Texts in Mathematics]]|first=P. R.|last=Halmos|authorlink=Paul Halmos|publisher=Springer|year=1960|isbn=9780387900926|page=32|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=x6cZBQ9qtgoC&pg=PA32}}.</ref>
* A function that sends an element <math>x</math> to its [[equivalence class]] under a specified [[equivalence relation]] <math>E,</math><ref>{{citation|title=An Introduction to Analysis|volume=154|series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics|first1=Arlen|last1=Brown|first2=Carl M.|last2=Pearcy|publisher=Springer|year=1995|isbn=9780387943695|page=8|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y2Mwck8Q9A4C&pg=PA8}}.</ref> or, equivalently, a [[surjection]] from a set to another set.<ref>{{citation|title=Set Theory: The Third Millennium Edition|series=Springer Monographs in Mathematics|first=Thomas|last=Jech|publisher=Springer|year=2003|isbn=9783540440857|page=34|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WTAl997XDb4C&pg=PA34}}.</ref> The function from elements to equivalence classes is a surjection, and every surjection corresponds to an equivalence relation under which two elements are equivalent when they have the same image. The result of the mapping is written as <math>[x]</math> when <math>E</math> is understood, or written as <math>[x]_E</math> when it is necessary to make <math>E</math> explicit.
